topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These introductory remarks welcome the students and outline the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional therapeutic modalities and their limitations, focusing on surgery, radiotherapy, cytotoxic chemotherapy, and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular defects and hormone dependence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe targeted therapeutic strategies designed to exploit cancer-specific biological vulnerabilities, such as hormone receptor reliance, cell cycle checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinases and overcoming resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the principles, molecular mechanisms, and resistance pathways associated with small-molecule kinase inhibitors targeting driver oncogenes.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover antibody-based therapeutic approaches that leverage cell-surface target specificity to block signaling pathways or selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Tumor immunology and immunotherapeutic strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for natural immune surveillance and explore clinical strategies to mobilize host T-cell responses against cancer.

topics.label: Current challenges, future directions, and therapeutic dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on broader paradigms in cancer management, addressing historical progress, early detection, and the ethical dilemmas of integrating novel therapies into clinical practice.
